body:
> converting the HashMap of physics quadrants to a AHashMap, to allow access by index as well as key, although it shouldn't affect existing functionality

Does it affect performance though?

This requires a proposal, I don't want to expose the thing for the sake of it. And tbh, those are internal optimization i'd rather avoid users rely on, as keeping compatibility later on ends up being a nightmare. so I think the use case has to be solid.

I've opened a [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12612) explaining my thoughts why this should be added

As for performance, I don't expect there to be any tangible difference, but I will try to do some comparisons

> > converting the HashMap of physics quadrants to a AHashMap, to allow access by index as well as key, although it shouldn't affect existing functionality
> 
> Does it affect performance though?

I decided to time `void TileMapLayer::_physics_update(bool p_force_cleanup)` since it's where the quadrant map is almost exclusively accessed. I threw together a small script to place/remove tiles with a simple full-square physics polygon (entirety of the tile is covered by the shape), as well as adjust the quadrant size. Repeated a few times to make sure there were no outliers.

As far as I can tell, there is no tangible perf difference, especially considering that virtually all of the time is spent on handling the polygons themselves.

[tilemap-chunk-compare.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20747207/tilemap-chunk-compare.zip)

I wouldnt expose it directly like that, at least not now while the internal merge is just fresh out from development and has barely been tested for real with users.

If this is exposed like this and you want to change the internal merge behavior you would immediatly run into the issue of breaking x-amount of spacebar heated projects.

Barely anyone tests beta version and we already have unsolved bug reports like this https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104452 open. The release will give a flood of bug reports related to polygon bool ops edge case that will likely require changes.

What the TileMap imo could and should do is expose "chunk" query functions for cells, e.g. get cells in Rect2. That would benefit all kinds of projects, addons and systems immediately and is generic enough to persist without compatibility issues. That the Geometry2D functions still cant support multi-polygon ops is its own issue.
